root_cause_label: Python 3.12 Incompatibility with Legacy SpinningUp v0.2.0 ML Stack
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent encountered Python 3.12 incompatibility with the legacy SpinningUp v0.2.0 stack (requiring TF<2.0 and torch==1.3.1) at step 11 and spent 49 subsequent steps thrashing through piecemeal dependency installs and source code patches that never completed a working environment.
t_err_evidence: pip install -e . attempts to pull matplotlib==3.1.1 and torch==1.3.1, incompatible with Python 3.12
t_commit_evidence: Step 11 reveals the core blocker: the legacy dependency stack (matplotlib 3.1.1, tensorflow<2.0, torch==1.3.1) is fundamentally unbuildable on Python 3.12. From this step forward, every subsequent attempt is recovery/patching — no complete working environment is ever achieved within 60 steps. The agent never pivots to the correct strategy (install compatible modern versions or use a legacy Python version), so failure is locked in.
t_surface_evidence: AttributeError: module 'configparser' has no attribute 'SafeConfigParser' building matplotlib==3.1.1 wheel
trigger_explanation: The agent faced a real environment obstacle (Python 3.12 missing old APIs used by legacy ML packages pinned in setup.py). Instead of pivoting to a working strategy at step 10 (after reading the problematic pins) or immediately at step 11 (after seeing the first build failure), the agent handled it incorrectly: it kept attempting to install individual legacy packages piece by piece, modifying setup.py pins slightly, trying to install Python 3.7 (unavailable), and finally performing incomplete source-code patches that made TF imports optional but never completed a runnable environment before the step budget ran out.
forewarning_evidence: The virtual environment was not created successfully because ensurepip is not available.
